title: dublin_node_street searches only a ±1-cell window but accepts streets up to 3.0 tiles away — nearby streets are invisible, blocks mis-orient
detail: Segments are bucketed only into cells their own bbox covers (x0..=x1 of the segment), but the lookup scans just the node's 3×3 cell neighborhood. A street 1–3 tiles away outside that window is never found: found=false fires the axis-aligned fallback plus a false 'no street within 3 tiles' log. Verified against data/maps/dublin.json with the sim's exact stride-6 int-snapped pool: 10 of 602 pool tiles have a street within 3.0 tiles (nearest 1.22 tiles, e.g. pool tile (19,15)) that this window never sees.
recommended_fix: Widen the search window to ±ceil(DUBLIN_SEG_MAX_DIST) cells (±3), or inflate each segment's bucket bbox by DUBLIN_SEG_MAX_DIST at build time; keep the ±1 fast path only if the max dist is lowered to ~1 tile.

title: The claimed 'one-shot' fallback log has no guard — it prints per node per frame from the render loop
detail: dublin_node_block_draw runs from draw_building every frame per terminal; there is no dedup/one-shot state, so every street-less node logs at frame rate. Reachable now: pool tile (23,16) has no street within 3 tiles, and the 10 window-missed tiles also set found=false — ~660 log lines/sec at 60fps once spawned.
recommended_fix: Gate the log with a per-node or per-position 'already flagged' set (or log only when found transitions), e.g. a small [dynamic]i32 of flagged node ids checked before printfln.

title: Dublin block path drops reveal_fade — the block body pops in at full opacity while the chip fades
detail: The sprite path fades the whole terminal during the 8-tick spawn reveal (alpha u8(255*clamp01(reveal_fade)) plus draw_family_wash fade); the Dublin branch passes only reveal_scale and dublin_node_block_draw has no reveal_fade parameter — 'col := fam' draws full-alpha, so new blocks pop while their chips fade.
recommended_fix: Add a reveal_fade parameter to dublin_node_block_draw and blend the block/edge alpha (col.a = u8(255*clamp01(fade))) like the sprite path.

title: build_sea silently returns an empty sea on five degenerate paths — the headline fix can regress to 'no Irish Sea' with no warning
detail: If OSM drift removes/re-tags coastline ways, the seed lands in a land face, or polygonize yields nothing, the bake succeeds with zero sea polygons and no error — exactly the user's original complaint, silently. Only the human-readable poly count hints at it.
recommended_fix: Raise (or at least loudly warn) when any of these paths yields no sea polygon — e.g. print '[bake] WARNING: sea construction empty' or sys.exit non-zero — and assert a minimum sea area at bake.

title: Committed Blender tool defaults to a hardcoded personal absolute worktree path when PP_WT is unset
evidence: WT = os.environ.get("PP_WT") or "/Users/moses/.herdr/worktrees/packet-plumber/packet-plumber-v2-dublin-map-beautify"  # the packet-plumber root (PP_WT overrides)
detail: Without PP_WT set, the committed tool reads/writes .scratch and assets/maps under a stale machine-specific path (silently creating directories there via os.makedirs) instead of failing; prep_board_geometry.py likewise uses unvalidated CWD-relative paths.
recommended_fix: Derive the repo root from __file__ (os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))))) and drop the hardcoded default; fail fast if the path isn't a repo root.
